name: RXO, Inc.
business: RXO brokers truckload freight and provides managed transportation, last mile and forwarding services to shippers in North America, Europe and Asia.

events.what: Acquired Coyote Logistics from UPS for $1.038B cash (+$10M post-close adjustment); outside the 18-month window
events.source: 10-K business description via Baba data_profile; no Item 2.01 8-K returned by sec-api

events.what: Chief Accounting Officer succession (internal); the only Item 5.02 8-K since 2024-07-01
CEO since spin-off from XPO (no change); CFO James Harris also in seat since the spin

next_event.source: No Investor Day or framework update found in Baba; last long-term targets were set at the 2022 Investor Day (pre-Coyote) and Wilkerson said in June 2024 'as we get closer, we'll roll something' (doc 68239). Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA guided $35M to $45M (doc 130108).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Through-cycle 'at least mid-single-digit' / 'at least a 5%' EBITDA margin stated by the Chief Strategy Officer, not the CEO or CFO, with no year. The Coyote synergy target ($70M cash: $60M opex, $10M capex) was set and mostly realized in 2025; CFO guided an incremental $10M of P&L benefit in 2026. Margin is driven by the freight cycle (truckload spot rates and gross profit per load), not a self-help program.

statements.quote: When we think about this business through cycle, I think it would be at least a mid-single-digit EBITDA margin business. That's prior to any type of advantage that we'll have as we think about deploying technology across the organization to lead to further productivity gains.
statements.speaker: Jared Weisfeld

statements.quote: You think about just getting volume back, more opportunities for gross profit per load and at least a 5% EBITDA-type margin. We're talking about a long runway from growth from current levels.
statements.speaker: Jared Weisfeld

statements.quote: We talked about around $70 million of synergies, 60 of which was to hit OpEx, 10 of which to hit CapEx. A majority of that has flown through the P&L in 2025. We see about an incremental $10 million of additional P&L realized in 2026 versus 2025 related to synergies alone.
statements.speaker: Jamie Harris

street.gap_assumption: No target year stated; 5% through-cycle EBITDA margin compared with the furthest consensus year, Baba FY2028 (calendar FY, labels match company years). Against FY2027 consensus (3.36%) the gap would be about 164 bps.

evidence_of_progress.note: VA adjusted EBITDA margin yoy: Q4 2025 -136 bps, Q1 2026 -111 bps (Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA $6M on $1.425B). VA has not loaded Q2 2026; per Harris Q2 2026 revenue was $1.8B and adjusted EBITDA $40M, above guidance (doc 130108). LTM 1.62% uses Q2 2025 to Q1 2026. Forward estimates are now rising fast: the 4-month EBITDA revision is +11.9% and the 4-month revenue revision +11.9%, on a supply-driven truckload tightening (spot mix 42%).

disqualifier_reason: Catalyst older than 18 months with no pending change: Coyote closed 2024-09-16 (24 months ago) and its $70M synergy target is mostly realized; CEO and CFO unchanged since the November 2022 spin, and the only in-window 5.02 is a CAO succession. Margin is set by the truckload freight cycle, and the 4-month forward EBITDA revision of +11.9% means the street is already moving (D = 0).
verdict: A freight-cycle recovery trade, not a GXO-style setup: no leadership change, Coyote is 24 months old, and estimates are already rising 12% in four months.
open_questions: Will management restate long-term targets post-Coyote, given the last set dates from the 2022 Investor Day?
How much of the +11.9% four-month EBITDA revision is spot-rate driven and reversible?
Does the Supreme Court Montgomery broker-liability case raise RXO's insurance cost or carrier vetting cost?
